A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHIFT. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVD and Wan2.2 fine-tuning experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations and qualitative generation results in the main paper and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds component analyses and a VisionReward evaluation of Wan2.2 variants in Appendices B and C.

M1.justification: The pixel-motion reward models, hybrid SFT/AWR objective, adversarial reward updates, noise alignment and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new experiment removing noise alignment is an ablation, not a revision of SHIFT.

E1.justification: Both versions retain DAVIS2017, WISA-80K deformation and VBench-I2V coverage for image-conditioned video generation. VisionReward introduces additional scoring, without identifying a new dataset, domain or generation task.

E2.justification: v1's Wan2.2 comparison contains Base, SFT and SHIFT in Table 2. v2 retains that table and adds a Wan2.2 VisionReward comparison including DenseDPO and FlowGRPO in Table A2. These methods were already SVD comparators; the SVD comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added VisionReward evaluation uses aggregate reward and macro yes-rates across 64 questions, including 36 Appearance and 8 Dynamic questions. v2 also adds an A4-minus-noise-alignment control and extended A3/A4 comparisons through epoch 9, while removing the 20K-step query-sampling classification evaluation. Retained experiment settings are unchanged; the new VLM evaluation's video set and sample count are unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a test isolating noise alignment within the full model and an extended-training analysis of whether adversarial reward updates prevent collapse. Conversely, v1's Appendix C comparison of random versus uniform-grid LMR query sampling is removed. The existing component, temperature, buffer-reuse and encoder ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's claim that Dynamic is 'statistically on par' supplies no supporting uncertainty analysis. Its A4 score range describes training dynamics, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 and the renamed encoder-ablation table retain their values. New Table A2 reports, for example, SHIFT reward 3.571 and Dynamic 45.30%, versus SFT 3.752 and 37.12%. v2 also adds noise-alignment removal results and A3's epoch-9 Overall score of 81.90. The random/grid accuracies of 0.88/0.75 reported in v1 are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, assumptions and derivations in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A are retained. Explicitly identifying the spatial domain as a subset of R² and explaining x0 clarify existing notation without changing the formal setup.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: pixel-motion rewards and sampler-agnostic hybrid fine-tuning improve motion while preserving appearance, with adversarial updates mitigating reward hacking. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets VisionReward as complementary confirmation and claims a uniquely balanced, near-Pareto outcome for SHIFT. It also extends the stabilization discussion using the new component analyses. The earlier foreground/background explanation for random query sampling is removed; the main motion–appearance and reward-hacking interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL but removes the H20-3e GPU identifiers from the configuration table, retaining the 64/128 GPU counts. LoRA, sampling, optimizer, buffer and reward-model configurations otherwise remain documented with the same values. The PDFs do not establish what resources the new URL provides.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Stable Video Diffusion, Wan, VPTR and STDiff, and removes the original CoTracker reference while retaining CoTracker3. These are limited contextual citation changes; the positioning against existing alignment methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and prose edits, clarifies notation, adds keywords, equal-contribution and acceptance notes, and acknowledgements. It inserts the VLM-evaluation appendix section and renumbers subsequent sections, while preserving the overall narrative and most wording.

P2.justification: v2 substantially narrows the text block and increases margins, rescaling and repositioning figures, tables and equations throughout the document. It adds Table A2 and adopts separate appendix display numbering. Existing qualitative images and plotted content are retained; the major change is the pervasive visual reformatting.

improvement.justification: The full-model noise-alignment control and extended A3/A4 analysis strengthen evidence for SHIFT's central stabilization mechanisms, while VisionReward adds complementary validation. This is a limited net gain: v2 removes query-sampling evidence and GPU model information, retains a reference to the removed sampling ablation, and uses unsupported 'statistically on par' wording. The method and main quantitative results remain unchanged.
